gaps.sentence: 'I can swim,' the boy boasted. The boy boasted that he ___ swim.
gaps.explanation: Can backshifts to could in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Don't touch the wet paint,' the caretaker warned us. The caretaker warned us ___ the wet paint.
gaps.explanation: Negative commands become not to + infinitive after told/asked/warned.

gaps.sentence: 'We may be a few minutes late,' they warned. They warned that they ___ be a few minutes late.
'What are your plans for the weekend?' he asked. He asked what my plans for the weekend ___.
gaps.explanation: are → were: the copula backshifts like any other verb.

gaps.sentence: 'I'd love to come,' she said. She said she ___ love to come.
gaps.explanation: 'I'd love' is I would love; would does not change in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'We'll be arriving on the red-eye,' they said. They said they ___ on the red-eye.
gaps.explanation: 'Will be arriving' backshifts to 'would be arriving'.

gaps.sentence: "We are leaving now." — They said they ___ then.
'Come round to my house tomorrow,' she said. She invited me round to her house ___.
gaps.explanation: Tomorrow becomes the next day (the following day) when the invitation is reported.
